title: Director's Statement on the Budget and Economic Outlook for 2026 to 2036
discussion_signal: The CBO announcement frames tariffs, lower immigration, fiscal policy, and the 2026–2036 baseline as interacting forces rather than isolated headlines. It makes a macroeconomic forecast socially legible as a question about labor supply, growth, prices, and institutional choices.
linked_research_question: How do policy choices around trade, immigration, aging, and AI reconfigure growth, fiscal room, and social expectations?
limits: A forecast is conditional on assumptions and is not an observed outcome
The official post does not expose a representative audience discussion
Macro aggregates do not resolve distributional effects
